name: Pam Marsh
website_verified_via: Linked in Marsh's pamphlet statement (Book 3, p. 40): https://representativepammarsh.com/

bio.statement: Marsh's pamphlet statement lists her occupation as Oregon State Representative for House District 5 (2017 to present).
bio.excerpt: Occupation: Oregon State Representative, House District 5 (2017-current)

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 3, p. 40)

bio.statement: She lists prior governmental experience on the Ashland City Council, Planning Commission and Charter Review Commission.
bio.excerpt: Prior Governmental Experience: Ashland City Council (2012-2016); Ashland Planning Commission (2006-2012); Ashland Charter Review Commission (2004-2006)

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 3, p. 40)

bio.statement: Her official page says she is serving a fifth term and chairs the House Committee on Housing and Homelessness.
bio.excerpt: I am honored to serve residents of southern Jackson County for a fifth term in the Oregon Legislature.

source.publisher: Oregon Legislature, Rep. Pam Marsh official page

bio.statement: Her official page lists her as chair of the House Committee on Housing and Homelessness.
bio.excerpt: I currently serve as Chair of the House Committee on Housing and Homelessness

source.publisher: Oregon Legislature, Rep. Pam Marsh official page

positions.statement: Marsh says that as housing committee chair she has championed efforts to accelerate affordable housing development.
positions.excerpt: As chair of the Housing and Homelessness Committee, I have championed efforts to accelerate affordable housing development, including modular production, senior housing initiatives, manufactured home affordability, shelter sustainability and funding options

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 3, p. 40)

positions.statement: Marsh says she advocated for wildfire mitigation funding and a home hardening program.
positions.excerpt: I advocated for new funding for wildfire mitigation and championed establishment of a home hardening program to assist residents in high risk wildfire areas.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 3, p. 40)

positions.statement: Marsh says she passed legislation requiring data centers to pay the full costs of the energy they use.
positions.excerpt: I passed legislation to ensure that data centers pay the full costs of the energy they use.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 3, p. 40)

positions.statement: Marsh lists long-term stability of Southern Oregon University and higher education institutions among her priorities.
positions.excerpt: My priorities include long-term stability of Southern Oregon University and our state’s higher education institutions

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 3, p. 40)

positions.statement: Marsh says she will continue to address protecting immigrant neighbors, stabilizing hospitals and strengthening schools and small businesses.
positions.excerpt: I will continue to address additional issues that confront us, including protecting our immigrant neighbors, stabilizing our hospitals and health care facilities, and strengthening our schools and small businesses.

source.publisher: Oregon Secretary of State, Voters' Pamphlet, General Election Nov. 3, 2026 (Book 3, p. 40)

positions.statement: Reported by the Portland Tribune, Marsh told colleagues many more people likely died in the heat dome and said she plans to convene a workgroup on cooling systems in housing.
positions.excerpt: told her colleagues that many more people likely died during the heat dome due to chronic and underlying medical conditions. She said she plans to convene a workgroup on the issue of providing cooling systems in housing.
